# Knots for sailors

A handful of knots covers almost everything on a sailing boat: tying sheets to the jib clew, securing the boat to a cleat on the dock, and reefing the mainsail. Practise them until your hands tie them in the dark. They hold the lines when [[Anchoring overnight]].

## Bowline

A fixed loop at the end of a line that never slips and unties easily after a heavy load. Used for jib sheets and mooring lines.

## Reef knot

Two half knots tied in opposite directions, used to tie the reef points of a reefed mainsail around the boom. Never use it to join two lines that carry load.

## Cleat hitch

Secures a line to a horn cleat: a full turn, a figure of eight over the horns, then a locking hitch.
